people.label: Edgar Fouche
people.sub: USAF master sergeant and avionics maintenance NCO, later a DoD contractor engineering manager; originating claimant of the TR-3B in an August 1998 presentation
people.narrative: Edgar Albert Fouche is the single named origin of the TR-3B account, and what makes him a node is that origin and not any documented authority. The ordinary facts of his life are settled at Tier 1: born 22 February 1948 in Americus, Georgia, died 11 May 2017 aged 69, buried at Coffey Cemetery in Mason County, Texas, and independently fixed at 1948 by the Library of Congress name authority attached to his own book. The career the opened records document is a twenty year enlisted avionics maintenance career: F-15 and F-16 manual test stations, the TEWS-TITE electronic warfare bay, a Strategic Air Command liaison post at Kelly AFB, a Community College of the Air Force associate degree in avionics systems technology, and three Meritorious Service Medals whose citations describe exactly that work. It is an honourable record and an entirely ordinary one, and nothing in it touches aerospace design, propulsion or physics. Everything extraordinary rests on his own word in documents he wrote and copyrighted himself: the Top Secret and 'Q' clearances, the descent from Napoleon's minister of police, the helicopter flights to Groom Lake, and the TR-3B. One document is a real counterweight and the node must carry it: an AF Form 77a of 24 August 1979 records him assigned temporary duty to AFFTC Detachment 3 on the Nellis range for ten weeks, and Peter Merlin, the historian whose analysis demolishes most of the rest of the account, is the source that identifies Detachment 3 AFFTC as the unit operating Groom Lake. That form also says its own limit out loud: his duties there 'have been verified via a separate report', and that separate report is not in the file. In July 1998 he published a novel with Brad Steiger; the Library of Congress catalogues it as science fiction. In August 1998 he gave the presentation that put the TR-3B into the world.
people.tierRationale: Node tier C: proximity to the programme, not credibility. Custody proximity 0 because no opened record places him near any material, article or craft. Access 1 rather than 0 because, uniquely among the claimants on this board, one Air Force form does record him temporarily assigned to the unit that operates Groom Lake; and 1 rather than higher because the same form describes the work as F-15 avionics intermediate shop maintenance and no clearance record, SAP or USAP access of any kind was opened. Disclosure role 3 because his entire documented function in this subject is publication, which matches the board's treatment of mark-mccandlish and steven-greer.

people.sub: Aerospace historian and aerospace archaeologist; author of nine books including three published by NASA and AIAA; the substantive named sceptic on Fouche's documents and photographs
people.narrative: Peter W. Merlin is on this board because he is the rare thing this subject almost never produces: a named, credentialed, checkable analyst who has gone through a claimant's own documents item by item. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Studies from Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, has researched Area 51 since 1984, co-founded the X-Hunters Aerospace Archeology Team, and has written or co-written nine books, three of them published by NASA and the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics. His four findings against Fouche are not opinion: each is a falsifiable specific about something outside Fouche's own testimony. He says the 'SAC-DARPA' letter carries no classification marking, which the page image corroborates. He says the aircraft Fouche captioned 'Have Blue' is the first YF-117A SENIOR TREND prototype. He says no person called Steve Stenson was ever commander of the Air Force Flight Test Center. He says the KGB props are fakes sold in surplus stores. He has not, so far as any opened record shows, been checked and found wrong. The reason he earns a node rather than a footnote is that he is on both sides of the same file: his own published reference work on Groom Lake is what identifies Detachment 3 of the Air Force Flight Test Center as the unit operating the airfield, and that identification is the only thing that makes Fouche's single best document mean anything at all.
people.tierRationale: Node tier C: he is an external analyst and historian, not an insider. Custody proximity 0 and access 0 because no opened record gives him clearance, office or contact with any programme material; he works from public and declassified records and from field archaeology. entities.label: TR-3B 'Astra', claimed black triangular aircraft
entities.sub: Claimed triangular craft described in one man's copyrighted August 1998 presentation; no record of its existence has been opened
entities.desc: The TR-3B is a CLAIMED craft for whose existence no record has been opened, and the board carries it as a claim and not as an object: every substantive description of it descends from a single named man's speaking script, which he copyrighted himself in August 1998 and which attributes the sighting itself to an unnamed friend. Everything on this node is therefore a description of a claim. One artefact carries that description and is why the node exists: the 62 page transcript headed 'Presentation to IUFOR by Edgar Rothshild Fouche / Copyright Aug. 1998 / Fouche Media Associates', in which slides 69 to 72 give the craft its designation and code name Astra, place it at Papoose, attribute it to 'the Top Secret, Aurora Program with SDI and black budget monies', name the National Reconnaissance Office, the NSA and the CIA as its funders and taskers, name Sandia and Livermore as developers of its propulsion, and specify 'a circular, plasma filled accelerator ring called the Magnetic Field Disrupter' running a 'mercury based' plasma 'pressurized at 250,000 atmospheres at a temperature of 150 degrees Kelvin and accelerated to 50,000 rpm'. THE DOCUMENT CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT THE SIZE OF THE CRAFT TWO SLIDES APART: slide 69 says 'The operational model is 600 feet across' and slide 70 says 'The 200 feet Prototype & the 300 feet Operational TR-3Bs are Code named Astra'. Both sentences are in the same document, in sequence, and nobody outside it has to adjudicate that. Three further things constrain this node. The presentation was given in the same summer as, and in order to promote, a book the Library of Congress catalogues as science fiction, LCCN 98002961, genre heading 'Science fiction.', subject 'Alien abduction - Fiction'. The propulsion specification is refuted by the freezing point of its own stated working fluid: NIST gives mercury a melting point of 234.31 K, and 150 K is 84 K below that. And the presentation's companion craft, the 'SR-75 Penetrator', is the name of a Testors plastic model kit of a speculative aircraft sold from 1993, five years earlier, about which the Air Force told the Baltimore Sun 'such a plane does not exist'.
entities.tierRationale: Node tier C: this is the thing claimed about, and nothing opened establishes it as an object. Custody proximity 0 and access 0 because there is no opened record of custody of, or access to, any article; disclosure role 3 because the node's entire documented footprint is in the disclosure literature. dateStart is the date of the originating artefact, August 1998, not an establishment date for anything. CRITICAL FOR ANY LATER CENTRALITY PASS: under the hub rule this node is the target of a claimant cluster whose dominant edge type is witness-chain, which CLAUDE.md section 6 deliberately excludes from PROGRAM_EDGES and counts at x1.0. A high degree on this node therefore means 'a lot is claimed here' and NEVER 'this is true'. Do not weight it otherwise and do not read its degree as corroboration.

claims.text: Stated inference, and it is a short one. 150 K is 84 K below mercury's melting point of 234.31 K at one atmosphere. Mercury's melting curve has a positive slope, so a pressure of 250,000 atmospheres raises the melting point rather than lowering it, putting the material further into the solid region and not closer to a gas. A plasma is an ionised gas. The specification therefore describes a solid and calls it a plasma, and it does so before any question of superconductivity, rotation or gravity is reached.

The MFD creates a disruption of the Earth's gravitational field upon the mass within the circular accelerator.' A magnetic field acting on gravitational mass is not a mechanism in any physical literature opened here, and the presentation gives no field strength, no power budget and no mass figure against which the claimed 89 per cent reduction could be checked. There is nothing in it to test, which is itself the finding.

It is a print of an HTML page, produced on 15 June 2014 with PDF-XChange, fifteen pages carrying 23 embedded images. Its text layer is caption and commentary rather than record, and the commentary is mixed-voice: some of it is a compiler's and some is Fouche's own, one passage being signed inside the text 'My guess is he was a Staff Sergeant judging by his skills. - Ed Fouche'. entities.label: AF Form 77a, Letter of Evaluation, 24 August 1979
entities.sub: The one document connecting Fouche to Groom Lake: a temporary duty assignment to AFFTC Detachment 3, Nellis AF Range, 1 June to 14 August 1979
entities.desc: THIS IS THE COUNTERWEIGHT AND IT MUST BE READ AS ONE. It is the strongest artefact in the entire Fouche thread, it is the only document that connects him to Groom Lake, and it should not be buried inside the compilation node. It is an AF Form 77a, a Supplemental Sheet to AF Forms 707, 909, 910, 911 and 475, stamped AUG 20 1979 and dated 24 August 1979, covering a period of observation from 10 June to 14 August 1979. The ratee is Fouche, Edgar A, active duty grade TSGT; the duty title is NCOIC F-15 AIS; the evaluator is Brewer, MSgt, USAF, 57 CRS, Nellis AFB Nevada. Its closing paragraph is the reason the node exists: 'OTHER COMMENTS: This out of cycle report is generated because TSgt Fouche was assigned TDY to the AFFTC-DET 3, Nellis AF Range from 1 June 79 to 14 August 79. His duties and responsibilities for this period have been verified via a separate report. RECOMMENDATION: Promote at the earliest opportunity.' Peter Merlin's own published reference work is what makes that mean anything: 'Since the late 1970s, the Groom Lake facility has been operated by Detachment 3 of the Air Force Flight Test Center.' AND THE FORM STATES ITS OWN LIMIT OUT LOUD. It does not say what he did while there; it refers that out to a separate report, and that separate report is not in the file. Everything else on the form describes conventional work: 'one of TACs best R&D team builders in areas of ECM, ATS, and cryptological support... the implementation of the TEWS-TITE bed-down, which was lauded by TAC Hq LGM... his MAJCOM involvement in cryptological asset training and provisioning'. A documented ten weeks of temporary duty at a documented secret airfield, doing F-15 avionics intermediate shop work, is a real and non-trivial fact. It is not a claim about a craft, and the claims about craft post-date it by a decade in the claimant's own telling.
entities.tierRationale: Node tier B: a dated, legible, specific primary personnel record naming a unit, a range, a rating official and a date range. Custody proximity 0 because temporary duty at an airfield is not custody of material. Access 1 rather than higher because the form records physical presence at the unit operating Groom Lake but describes the work as F-15 avionics intermediate shop maintenance, and no clearance, SAP or USAP access appears on it or anywhere in the collection; the axis is what access is documented, not what is claimed. Disclosure role 2 because this single page is what the whole credibility argument on both sides eventually turns on.

entities.label: Testor Corp. SR-75 Penetrator and XR-7 Thunderdart model kits, 1993
entities.sub: Commercially published speculative model kits designed by John Andrews whose designations reappear in Fouche's 1998 presentation as inside knowledge
entities.desc: This node exists because it is the only documented prior-art channel found for any part of the Fouche account, and because it is documented on both ends. On 25 December 1993 the Baltimore Sun reported that Testor Corp. was selling 'the SR-75 Penetrator and XR-7 Thunderdart, the latest in a series of highly speculative military miniature models', designed by 'John Andrews, an aviation historian in San Diego who designed the new models, as well as the F-19', and said to have been developed by analysing sonic boom patterns over Southern California, jet exhaust patterns over Nevada, published stealth and high-speed literature and industry speculation. The same article carries the Air Force on the record through its spokeswoman Capt. Mary Dillon: 'We're not saying no comment, we're saying such a plane does not exist.' Four and a half years later Fouche's presentation devotes slides 62 onward to an 'SR-75' called the 'Penetrator' that is also 'a mothership', and elsewhere to an 'SR-74 Scramp'. The designation and the mothership architecture are the same, the priority is documented and one-directional, and the direction of influence is not established. The node is here so that a build session cannot accidentally let the TR-3B cluster imply the reverse.

entities.label: Northrop TACIT BLUE
entities.sub: Declassified USAF, DARPA and Northrop stealth demonstrator; first flight February 1982, 135 flights, curved rather than faceted, on museum display since 1996
entities.desc: TACIT BLUE is on this board as the control case for the TR-3B, and its edge to the claim is a denial edge and not a supporting one. It is a real black programme of the right era, run by the right agencies, and its published record is precisely what the claim is not. The U.S. Air Force's own fact sheet states that 'The USAF, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, and the Northrop Corp. worked together from 1978 to 1985 to demonstrate that curved surfaces on an aircraft result in a low radar return signal from ground radar.' The aircraft made its first flight in February 1982 and had flown 135 times by the conclusion of the programme in 1985. It was placed on museum display in May 1996. Its span is 48 feet 2 inches, its length 55 feet 10 inches, its height 10 feet 7 inches, its weight 30,000 pounds, its powerplant two Garrett ATF3-6 high-bypass turbofans, and its armament none. THE POINT OF THE NODE: it is not triangular, its defining feature is curved surfaces, it is 48 feet across rather than 200 to 600, and it was retired before the TR-3B is claimed to have flown. The brief that produced this build asked for the widely reported analysis that the TR-3B narrative derives from or is confused with TACIT BLUE; that analysis was searched for and NOT FOUND, and the primary record argues against it. The documented aircraft that is close to triangular in planform and that did fly out of Groom Lake in the period is the F-117, which is the airframe Peter Merlin identifies in Fouche's own misattributed photograph.
entities.tierRationale: Node tier B: a fully documented, declassified programme with a primary government fact sheet, on public display, and directly adjacent to the claim by era, agencies and airfield. Custody proximity 1 and access 2 because this is a genuine compartmented development programme with real articles and real access control, in contrast to every claim node in this cluster; not 3 because it is long declassified and publicly exhibited. Disclosure role 2 because its 1996 unveiling is part of how the real black-aircraft record was opened.

This is what a real black aircraft programme of the era looks like in the primary record: 48 ft 2 in span, curved surfaces, two Garrett turbofans, no armament.
timeline.source: U.S. Air Force Fact Sheet 'NORTHROP TACIT BLUE', https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB443/docs/area51_58.PDF

timeline.label: The letter Fouche later calls the 'SAC/DARPA Classified Document' is written
timeline.text: A Headquarters Strategic Air Command letter of 10 July 1984, 'REPLY TO ATTN OF: DARPA', addressed to office code LGMQ, states 'HQ AFMPC has approved an AAR 51[redacted] on MSgt (32674) Fouche as requested. MSgt Fouche's date of availability is Aug 87.' It is signed by DALE E. HAGERMAN, TSgt, USAF, NCOIC, Amn Acft Maint Asgns Sec, Dir of Asgns, DCS/Pers. The page image carries no classification marking of any kind, and all redactions on it were applied by Fouche himself on his own caption's admission.
timeline.source: Page 1 image of https://www.checktheevidence.com/pdf/Edgar%20Fouches%20Military%20Documents.pdf , rendered at 190 dpi and read

timeline.label: End of Fouche's Strategic Air Command liaison post at Kelly AFB; active service concludes
timeline.text: The Meritorious Service Medal citation with oak leaf cluster reads 'as the Strategic Air Command Liaison Officer, San Antonio Air Logistics Center, Kelly Air Force Base, Texas, from 17 July 1983 to 31 August 1987', and closes 'The singularly distinctive accomplishments of Sergeant Fouche culminate a distinguished career in the service of his country.' The certificate is signed by John T. Chain, Jr., General, USAF, Commander in Chief.

timeline.label: Baltimore Sun reports the Testors SR-75 Penetrator and XR-7 Thunderdart on sale
timeline.text: 'Testor Corp. released the SR-75 Penetrator and XR-7 Thunderdart, the latest in a series of highly speculative military miniature models', designed by 'John Andrews, an aviation historian in San Diego who designed the new models, as well as the F-19'. The Air Force spokeswoman Capt. Mary Dillon is quoted: 'We're not saying no comment, we're saying such a plane does not exist.' Fouche's presentation of August 1998 presents the same SR-75 Penetrator designation and the same mothership architecture as inside knowledge.

timeline.label: TACIT BLUE placed on public museum display
timeline.text: 'The aircraft was placed on display at the museum in May 1996.' A real compartmented aircraft programme of the Groom Lake era ends in a public exhibition hall with a published fact sheet and a cockpit plaque naming its five pilots.
timeline.source: U.S. Air Force Fact Sheet 'NORTHROP TACIT BLUE', https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB443/docs/area51_58.PDF

timeline.label: THE ANCHOR: the presentation transcript that originates the TR-3B
timeline.text: A 62 page slide-cued speaking script headed 'Presentation to IUFOR by / Edgar Rothshild Fouche / Copyright Aug. 1998 / Fouche Media Associates'. Slide 5 names the book it was given to promote. Slides 69 to 72 give the TR-3B its designation and code name Astra, attribute it to 'the Top Secret, Aurora Program with SDI and black budget monies', name the NRO, NSA and CIA as funders and taskers, name Sandia and Livermore as developers of the propulsion, specify a mercury-based plasma 'at a temperature of 150 degrees Kelvin', and give the operational craft two different sizes two slides apart, 600 feet at slide 69 and 300 feet at slide 70.
timeline.source: Presentation to IUFOR by Edgar Rothshild Fouche, https://www.checktheevidence.com/pdf/Edgar%20Fouche%20-%201998%20Presentation%20to%20IUFOC.pdf

timeline.label: The most-reproduced black triangle photograph is confessed as a hoax on Belgian television
timeline.text: Robert Sheaffer records that on 26 July 2011 the Belgian broadcaster RTL carried the photographer's confession about the Petit-Rechain image of the 1989-90 Belgian wave: 'The UFO of Petit-Rechain is not a spaceship from a distant galaxy but a panel of painted styrofoam with three spots affixed', and, from the maker, 'One has managed to fool the whole world with a silly model made of styrofoam.' Fouche's 1998 presentation had attached his craft to 'the country of Belgium' at slide 6. This does not touch the eyewitness reports and it decides nothing about Fouche; it records that the visual corpus the claim borrows plausibility from has a confessed hoax at its centre.

timeline.label: The fifteen page military documents compilation is printed to PDF
timeline.text: The PDF opened carries producer 'PDF-XChange 4.0.195.0' and creation date D:20140615084520+01'00'. It is a print of an HTML page on checktheevidence.co.uk, 15 pages with 23 embedded images and a caption text layer in mixed voice. timeline.source: PDF metadata and contents read from https://www.checktheevidence.com/pdf/Edgar%20Fouches%20Military%20Documents.pdf

gaps.text: HIGHEST-VALUE GAP ON THIS LEAD. It was NOT established that Edgar Fouche ever stood at an International UFO Congress podium. The contemporaneous programme for the 7th Annual International UFO Congress Convention gives 1 to 7 February 1998 at the Gold River Resort, Laughlin, Nevada, and lists 24 speakers, none of whom is Fouche. His own transcript is headed 'Copyright Aug. 1998' and his own text says he spoke at Laughlin 'in August'; the Congress ran summer sessions separately from its February convention, so August is consistent rather than contradictory. But no contemporaneous programme, report, ticket or press notice placing him on any podium in 1998 was opened. The venue attribution the entire literature repeats rests on his own document header and on later repetition of it. This is the same shape as the McCandlish National Press Club finding in the ARV dossier.
gaps.wouldClose: A programme, flyer or convention report for the International UFO Congress summer sessions of August 1998; the International UFO Congress's own video archive at internationalufocongress.vhx.tv; or a contemporaneous newsletter from MUFON or a Laughlin-area paper.

gaps.text: RECORDED AGAINST THE BRIEF SO THE NEXT SESSION DOES NOT REDO IT. The brief asked for the widely reported analysis that the TR-3B narrative derives from or is confused with the real Northrop TACIT BLUE. That analysis was searched for and NOT FOUND, and the primary record argues against it: the USAF fact sheet's defining feature is curved surfaces, the aircraft is 48 ft 2 in across against a claimed 200 to 600 feet, and the programme concluded in 1985 against a craft claimed to have first flown in the early 1990s. There is no shape, size or date correspondence. The northrop-tacit-blue to tr-3b edge is therefore a denial edge and exists specifically to prevent the supportive version being drawn later. The conflation the record does support is with the F-117, which is Peter Merlin's identification of the airframe in Fouche's own misattributed photograph.
gaps.wouldClose: Nothing needs closing unless a source actually making that argument is produced; if one is, it should be read against the fact sheet before any edge is changed.
